name: Light Greenish Blue
lede: Light Greenish Blue joins the modifiers *light* and *greenish* to the base color [[blue]], and in our archive of 23,781 paintings not one canvas carries it.

sections.title: A compound, not a tradition
sections.body:
The name follows plain modifier grammar: *light greenish* plus [[blue]], first recorded in the xkcd 2010 crowd color survey and carried into our library from there [1]. Paterson's dictionary never lists "Light Greenish Blue" as a headword, but it uses the near-identical phrase "light greenish-blue" or "light greenish blue" to describe several other named colors: Aqua, aqua blue, horizon blue, and the older word glaucous [2]. That repetition across unrelated entries is a sign the phrase is descriptive shorthand, used whenever a writer needs a pale, green-leaning blue, rather than a single coined name with its own history [2].

The nearest ISCC-NBS 1955 block is "very light green," a Delta-E of 8.6 from this hex, which is a wide gap for a name that calls itself blue [1]. The nearest colors on file by measured distance are [[greenish-cyan]] and [[aquamarine]], 2.9 and 3.3 units away, with [[seafoam]] close behind at 3.3 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least one per cent of its canvas, within a Delta-E of 4, as photographed [3]. That describes the gap in this particular archive, not the color in painting generally: a crowd-survey name this bright and this pale rarely survives varnish and photography intact [3].
